title: Bob James One
hook: Nautilus lives on a 1974 record under 20 dollars.
voiceover: Nautilus lives on a 1974 record under 20 dollars. Bob James, One, CTI Records, 1974. Last track on side 2 is Nautilus. That bass and electric piano is under Ghostface's Daytona 500, Slick Rick's Children's Story, Run-DMC's Beats to the Rhyme, and that's a short list. CTI pressed a lot of these, so originals turn up everywhere for less than a takeout order. What to look for. The gatefold with the CTI logo, and check the run-out groove for the Van Gelder stamp, because Rudy Van Gelder mastered most of that catalog and those copies play loud. Send this to the friend who still buys vinyl. What's the record you'd never sell?
caption: Bob James, One (CTI, 1974). The last track, Nautilus, is under Ghostface's Daytona 500, Slick Rick's Children's Story, Run-DMC's Beats to the Rhyme and a long list after that. CTI pressed plenty, so this is a common record with an uncommon amount of rap history inside it. Look for the gatefold and the Van Gelder stamp in the dead wax. What's the record you'd never sell? 🎧
